newsitem.title: USA: Xerox buys rest of Rank-Xerox, suspends share buyback.
newsitem.headline: Xerox buys rest of Rank-Xerox, suspends share buyback.

text.p: Xerox Corp. announced Friday that it was buying the remaining 20 percent stake in its 41-year-old Rank Xerox office equipment joint venture from its partner, Britain's Rank Group Plc, for $1.5 billion.
Xerox suspended a $1 billion stock buyback programme to help fund the acquisition.
The purchase gives Stamford, Conn.-based Xerox sole ownership of the venture, based in Britain, which will be renamed Xerox Ltd. when the deal closes, the company said.

Xerox and Rank, a leisure and entertainment company, said Xerox would pay 500 million pounds ($812.6 million) on completion of the transaction, expected to take place at the end of June. The balance will be payable in two annual instalments of 220 million pounds ($358 million).
Xerox may pay another 60 million pounds ($98 million) in 2000, based on profit performance by 1999, the companies said.
The transaction has been approved by boards of both companies, Xerox said.

"Use of the company's financial resources to fund this $1.5 billion transaction produces greater value to Xerox shareholders than continuing the current share repurchase programme," Xerox Chairman Paul Allaire said.
"However, we will revist the share repurchase programme in the future," he added.
The stock repurchase plan was authorised in February 1996. By March 31, Xerox had bought back 8.2 million shares for $406 million, including $100 million in the first quarter of 1997.
Rank said Friday it intended to repurchase its own shares up to a maximum value of 250 million pounds ($407 million).

The London-based company said it expected to launch a stock buyback later this year and would use the balance of the initial payment from Xerox to cut debt and invest in its leisure and entertainment businesses.

Rank Xerox, formed in 1956, is based in Marlow, United Kingdom, and manufactures Xerox products, systems and supplies to market in more than 80 companies in Europe, Asia and Africa. The venture also owns a 50 percent stake in Fuji Xerox.
Xerox stock rose $1.125 to $67.75 in consolidated morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Trading in the stock was briefly halted for the announcement.
